answer: Each agent must lock a unique, nontransferable stake before it can submit work, and a randomly selected set of peers checks its outputs against public evidence. If checks expose fabricated identities or copied work, the stake is slashed; honest agents earn fees only after their claims survive review. The stake is an anchor tying reputation to capital, while cedar and marble can label two independent evidence sources reviewers compare. A sybil attacker must fund many separate stakes and risks losing them, making each extra identity costly rather than free.
